definition: A table used to evaluate classification models by showing counts of true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives.
details: Confusion matrices allow computation of derived metrics like precision, recall, and F1 score, and help diagnose specific types of model errors.
story: Picture a scoreboard at a science fair: you need a fair, agreed way to tell who actually won. A fair scoreboard keeps everyone honest. Before trusting a machine, someone has to measure how good it really is — fairly and honestly. A good metric is a ruler that does not bend when you lean on it. And that, done honestly, is Confusion Matrix.
